senses: Characterised by festivity and the celebration of love and/or drinking; bacchanalian, amorous.
ety: From Late Latin Anacreonticus, from Ancient Greek Ἀνακρέων (Anakréōn), Anacreon a Greek poet.

senses: Serving to declare or explain
A venue for motor racing.
examples: The motorplex, which also has tracks for motocross and all-terrain vehicles, has an overwhelmingly local feel.

senses: A neume representing a single tone.
ety: From Latin pūnctum. Doublet of point, pointe, ponto, puncto, punt, and punto.

senses: A device that generates artificial fog or smoke for stage performances.
A device that releases an insecticidal mist.
A Korean stew, typically made with meat, seafood or vegetables in a seasoned broth and served boiling hot.
ety: Borrowed from Korean 찌개 (jjigae), from 찌- (jji-, “to steam”) + -개 (-gae, suffix denoting something small associated with an action).

senses: An offering to God, especially in fulfilment of a vow.
An alms basket; a vessel to receive gifts of charity; a treasury of the church, where offerings are deposited.
ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κορβᾶν (korbân), borrowed from Biblical Hebrew קָרְבָּן (qɔrbɔn). Found in the Bible at Mark 7.11. Doublet of Qurbana.

senses: trouble; problem.
ety: From Yoruba wàhálà, from Hausa wàhalā̀, from Arabic وَهْلَة (wahla, “fright, terror”).
examples: Oscar flashed me another bent grin, palmed a pistol from under the seat and said, "First time in Nigeria? No wahalla, you are always protected sa."

senses: An unrefined brown sugar with a strong flavour of molasses.
ety: Corrupted from Spanish mascabado or Portuguese mascavado, from the verb mascavar, a corrupted form of menoscabar (“to despise”).

senses: Rather smart
The socioeconomic system based upon the industrial production of manufactured goods, rather than on agriculture.
A tool used to seal something.
A person who is employed to seal things.
An officer responsible for sealing writs or instruments, stamping weights and measures, etc.
A coating designed to prevent excessive absorption of finish coats into porous surfaces; a coating designed to prevent bleeding.
A bot that sends any type of spam content on the Internet, particularly originally mass junk email.
A traditional Spanish unit of mass, equivalent to about 50 mg.
ety: From Spanish grano (“grain, 1/9216 Spanish pound”), from Latin grānus (“grain”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵr̥h₂nóm. Doublet of grain.

senses: A young or little king.
Any of several birds of the family Regulidae.
The trade of manipulating materials in order to construct, install, and/or repair buildings or other structures.
The trade of cutting and joining wood, timber, or lumber; woodworking.
A carpenter’s workshop.
A collection of timber connected by being framed together, as the pieces of a roof, floor, etc.; work done by a carpenter.
ety: From Middle English carpentrie, from Anglo-Norman carpenterie, from Old Northern French (compare French charpenterie). See carpenter.

senses: Either of the two legs towards the front of a four-legged animal such as a horse, or towards the front of a many-legged animal such as most insects, or of a piece of furniture, etc.
The back of the neck.
ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin nuchālis, from nucha + -ālis, from Arabic نُخَاع (nuḵāʕ, “spinal cord”).

senses: The use of voice and gestures in oratory; the style of delivery of a speech.
Characterized by interdependence and a sense of mutual identity.
The act of enclosing in a capsule; the growth of a membrane around (any part) so as to enclose it in a capsule.
described or represented in a lifelike manner
One who is deceased, or will shortly become so.
examples: I could tell he was a deader by the way his eyes were glazed over; there was no life left in those eyes.

senses: The accumulated legislation and decisions of any international community.
ety: Shortened from acquis communautaire: French acquis (“that has been acquired or obtained”) + communautaire (“of the community”).

senses: One who brings deliverance.
A student of a prep school.
An anon; a user who posts anonymously on the Internet.
The person responsible for preventing and treating physical damage to a fighter between rounds of a match.
One who fishes with a creel.
Artificial rockwork made of rough stones and cement, as for gardens.
The rococo system of scroll ornament, based in part on the forms of shells and water-worn rocks.
A seed bead.
A valley between dunes.
ety: Borrowed from Afrikaans straat. Doublet of street.
examples: The "straate" are generally level and have a fairly hard surface often broken by protruding boulders of limestone.
Dune veld consists for the most part of rolling sand hills with wide or narrow straaten running in between the rows of sand hills.

senses: Without semantic content; lacking meaning.
examples: The asemic text, by definition, cannot be “decoded”, for the whole point of it is that there isn't any code, so the “reader” has to encode it.

senses: The scientific study of wines and winemaking.
Overgrown with jungle.
examples: He was lying on a bamboo bed in the traditional doctor's hut at the jungliest edge of the village.

senses: A knowledgeable or wise person; sage, saint.
ety: Borrowed from Hindi ज्ञानी (jñānī), from Sanskrit ज्ञानी (jñānī). Distantly related to know.
examples: He made friends with the pandits and gyanis and would sit with them for hours.
There is an abode called mah lok where highly evolved gyanis and yogis go but they are again reborn on the earth planet.

senses: An artist working in the style of pictorialism.
One who subscribes to the theory of pictorialism regarding mental imagery.
A flat talisman, almost always star-shaped, made of parchment, sheet metal, or other substance, marked with a magic symbol or symbols, used in magical evocation.
ety: From Middle French pentacle, from Old French pentacol (“pendant”), from pent (“hangs”), a (“from”), and col (“neck”), thus "hangs from neck". Likely reanalyzed in medieval times as coming from penta- (“five”) and -culum (object forming suffix), as evidenced by the Latinized form pentaculum and the narrowing of the modern sense to a five-pointed design, especially a pentagram.

senses: The status or rank of a nuncio (diplomatic representative of the Roman Catholic Church).
The building and staff of a nuncio; the equivalent of an embassy for the Holy See.
The term of service of a nuncio.
ety: From Latin nūnciāre, nūntiāre (“to announce, report”), from nūncius, nūntius (“messenger”). Compare French nonciature, Italian nunziatura.
examples: Seeing as the meeting happened at the nunciature in Washington, it could only have happened with the approval and participation of the nuncio, Archbishop Carlo Maria Vigano.

The Warsaw nuncio was content to preach a spirit of peace, and was severely taken to task by the Polish press during the summer of 1920. This cast something of a shadow over the final period of his nunciature.

senses: An artificial cloud made by the exhaust of jet aircraft or wingtip vortices that precipitate a stream of tiny ice crystals in moist, frigid upper air.
An evergreen tree, Dimocarpus longan, of the Sapindaceae family, native to southern China.
The fruit from the longan tree.
ety: Borrowed from Cantonese 龍眼 /龙眼 (lung⁴ ngaan⁵, literally “dragon’s eye”). Doublet of Longyan (“grape”).
